regulator: FAA Table B min = 540 min (9h00); EASA Table 2 min = 540 min (9h00) - IDENTICAL
measurement: Hanecke 1998 (1.2M German accidents, 1994): 'exponentially increasing accident risk beyond the 9th hour at work'
note: 540 min = 9.0 h exactly. Two regulators, independently, floor at the hour where the measured curve turns exponential.

test: floor moves EARLIER for late starts
regulator: FAA: 0000-0359 start caps at 540 min at ALL segment counts. EASA: 1700-0459 start reaches 540 min by 6 sectors.
measurement: Hanecke 1998: 'with later starting times, the relative accident risk increased dramatically beyond the 8th hour at work'
note: Both tables shorten the permitted duty as start time moves into the night; the measured knee also moves 9th->8th hour.

regulator: FAA 14 CFR 117.27: max THREE consecutive FDPs infringing the WOCL (five only with >=2h in-flight rest)
measurement: Folkard & Tucker 2003 (7 studies): risk vs 1st night = +6% (2nd), +17% (3rd), +36% (4th)
note: The regulator forbids exactly the shift that carries the +36% step. The cap lands on the knee, not before it.

measurement: Connor 2002: driving 0200-0500 vs other times, adjusted OR 5.6 (1.4-22.7)
note: The regulator's defined trough and the measured crash-risk trough are the same clock band.

test: which axis dominates - CIRCADIAN vs TASK DENSITY
regulator: FAA sheds 300 min for circadian vs 150 min for density (circadian DOMINATES 2:1). EASA sheds 120 min for circadian vs 240 min for density (density DOMINATES 2:1).
measurement: Connor 2002: circadian OR 5.6. No published study measures 'flight segments' as an exposure, so task density has NO effect size in this corpus.
note: The two regulators INVERT each other on which axis matters more. This is a genuine disagreement between published priors and the corpus cannot adjudicate it.

test: Van Dongen threshold vs regulator ceilings
regulator: FAA max FDP 840 min (14h00); EASA max 780 min (13h00); FMCSA driving window 840 min (14h00)
measurement: Van Dongen 2003: PVT lapses near-linear in cumulative wakefulness IN EXCESS OF 15.84 h (s.e. 0.73 h) = 950 min (s.e. 44 min)
note: Duty length is not time-since-waking. Converting one to the other requires assuming a pre-duty awake interval, which no source in this corpus measures. LOAD-BEARING JUDGEMENT - see report.
